And he took six hundred choice chariots
and all [the other] chariots of Egypt,
and officers upon all of them.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְחַזֵּ֣ק יְהֹוָ֗ה אֶת־לֵ֤ב פַּרְעֹה֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם
pairs.english: And the L-rd strengthened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt [Pharaoh wavering between pursuing and not pursuing]
and he pursued the children of Israel,
and the children of Israel went out with a high hand [i.e., with manifest might].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּרְדְּפ֨וּ מִצְרַ֜יִם אַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ם וַיַּשִּׂ֤יגוּ אוֹתָם֙ חֹנִ֣ים עַל־הַיָּ֔ם
pairs.english: And Egypt pursued them, and they overtook them camping by the sea,
every horse of Pharaoh's chariots and his horsemen and his host,
by Pi Hachiroth, before Baal Tzefon.
And Pharaoh pressed ahead [of the others],

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׂאוּ֩ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל אֶת־עֵינֵיהֶ֜ם וְהִנֵּ֥ה מִצְרַ֣יִם ׀ נֹסֵ֣עַ אַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ם
pairs.english: and the children of Israel lifted their eyes, and, behold, Egypt coming after them [with one heart, as one man],
and they were exceedingly afraid,
and the children of Israel cried out to the L-rd, ["embracing the trade" (prayer) of their fathers: (Abraham — Genesis 19:27; Isaac — 24:63; Jacob — 28:11)].
And they said to Moses:

pairs.hebrew: הֲֽמִבְּלִ֤י אֵין־קְבָרִים֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם לְקַחְתָּ֖נוּ לָמ֣וּת בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר
pairs.english: Is it for lack of graves in Egypt that you have taken us to die in the desert!
What is this that you did to us to take us out of Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: הֲלֹא־זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁר֩ דִּבַּ֨רְנוּ אֵלֶ֤יךָ בְמִצְרַ֙יִם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר
pairs.english: Is not this the thing that we spoke to you in Egypt [5:21], saying:
Let us be and let us serve Egypt,

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י ט֥וֹב לָ֙נוּ֙ עֲבֹ֣ד אֶת־מִצְרַ֔יִם מִמֻּתֵ֖נוּ בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
pairs.english: for it is better for us to serve Egypt than to die in the desert.
And Moses said to the people: Do not fear.

pairs.hebrew: הִֽתְיַצְּב֗וּ וּרְאוּ֙ אֶת־יְשׁוּעַ֣ת יְהֹוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם הַיּ֑וֹם
pairs.english: Stand ready to see the salvation of the L-rd, which He shall work for you this day.
For your seeing Egypt is [only] this day;
you shall see them no more, forever.
The L-rd will war for you,
and you will be still.
And the L-rd said to Moses:
Why do you cry out to Me? [i.e., Why do you prolong your prayer when Israel are stepped in affliction?]
Speak to the children of Israel and have them go forward [(There is nothing standing in their way. The merits of their fathers and their belief in Me will suffice to split the sea.)]
And you, raise your staff,
and stretch out your hand over the sea, and split it.
And the children of Israel shall come in the midst of the sea on the dry land.
And I, behold, I shall strengthen the heart of Egypt,
and they shall come after them,
and I shall be glorified through Pharaoh and through all his host, through his chariots and through his horsemen.
And Egypt will know that I am the L-rd
when I am glorified through Pharaoh, through his chariots and through his horsemen.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּסַּ֞ע מַלְאַ֣ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים הַהֹלֵךְ֙ לִפְנֵי֙ מַחֲנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ מֵאַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And the angel of G-d (Elokim), who went before the camp of Israel, turned and went behind them [to separate the Israelites from the Egyptians and to receive the projectiles intended for them. ("Elokim" connotes justice. Israel was being judged at that moment for survival or for destruction along with the Egyptians)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּסַּ֞ע עַמּ֤וּד הֶֽעָנָן֙ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֔ם וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד מֵאַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃
pairs.english: And [when it became dark and the pillar of fire supervened], the pillar of cloud turned from before them and stood behind them [to "darken things" for the Egyptians].

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֞א בֵּ֣ין ׀ מַחֲנֵ֣ה מִצְרַ֗יִם וּבֵין֙ מַחֲנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל
pairs.english: And it came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel.
And there was a cloud and darkness [for the Egyptians] and it [the pillar of fire] lighted the night [for the Israelites],
and the one [camp] did not come close to the other all the night.
And Moses stretched his hand over the sea,

pairs.hebrew: וַיּ֣וֹלֶךְ יְהֹוָ֣ה ׀ אֶת־הַ֠יָּ֠ם בְּר֨וּחַ קָדִ֤ים עַזָּה֙ כׇּל־הַלַּ֔יְלָה
pairs.english: and the L-rd drove the sea with a strong east wind [(the strongest of the winds)] all the night,
and He made the sea into dry land,
and the waters [of all the world] were split.
And the children of Israel came in the midst of the sea on the dry land.
And the water was to them a wall, on their right and on their left.
And Egypt pursued and came behind them,

pairs.hebrew: כֹּ֚ל ס֣וּס פַּרְעֹ֔ה רִכְבּ֖וֹ וּפָרָשָׁ֑יו אֶל־תּ֖וֹךְ הַיָּֽם׃
pairs.english: all horse of Pharaoh [i.e., all of his horses being regarded as (only) one in the eyes of the L-rd], his chariot and his riders into the midst of the sea.
And it was in the morning watch

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּשְׁקֵ֤ף יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מַחֲנֵ֣ה מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּעַמּ֥וּד אֵ֖שׁ וְעָנָ֑ן
pairs.english: that the L-rd looked to the camp of Egypt [to destroy it] with a pillar of fire and cloud [(The pillar of cloud rendered the sea-bed clay, and the pillar of fire made it so hot that the horses' hooves fell off)],
and He confounded the camp of Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֗סַר אֵ֚ת אֹפַ֣ן מַרְכְּבֹתָ֔יו וַֽיְנַהֲגֵ֖הוּ בִּכְבֵדֻ֑ת
pairs.english: And He removed their chariot wheels [(They were burnt off, the chariots jolted, and the drivers were broken)], and He led them with [the measure of] hardness, [measure for measure for their hardness (9:34)].
And Egypt said: I shall flee from before Israel;
for the L-rd wars for them against the Egyptians.
And the L-rd said to Moses:
Stretch forth your hand over the sea
so that the waters [standing like a wall] return [to their place] upon Egypt, upon its chariot, and upon its riders.
And Moses stretched forth his hand upon the sea,
and the sea returned towards morning to its [original] strength,
and Egypt [in distraction] fled towards it,
and the L-rd shook out Egypt into the midst of the sea.
And the waters returned and covered the chariot and the riders

pairs.hebrew: לְכֹל֙ חֵ֣יל פַּרְעֹ֔ה הַבָּאִ֥ים אַחֲרֵיהֶ֖ם בַּיָּ֑ם
pairs.english: of all the host of Pharaoh that came after them in the sea;
not so much as one remained of them.

pairs.hebrew: וּבְנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הָלְכ֥וּ בַיַּבָּשָׁ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ הַיָּ֑ם
pairs.english: And the children of Israel walked on the dry land in the midst of the sea.
And the water was to them a wall, on their right and on their left.

pairs.hebrew: וַיּ֨וֹשַׁע יְהֹוָ֜ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֛וּא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִיַּ֣ד מִצְרָ֑יִם
pairs.english: And the L-rd saved Israel on that day from the hand of Egypt,

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֤רְא יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת־מִצְרַ֔יִם מֵ֖ת עַל־שְׂפַ֥ת הַיָּֽם׃
pairs.english: and Israel saw Egypt dead on the shore of the sea, [the Egyptians having been cast up there so that Israel not say: Just as we came up on this side, so they came up on another side and will pursue us].

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֨רְא יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־הַיָּ֣ד הַגְּדֹלָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֤ה יְהֹוָה֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם
pairs.english: And Israel saw the great hand by which the L-rd wrought against Egypt,
and the people feared the L-rd,
and they believed in the L-rd and in Moses, His servant.

pairs.hebrew: אָ֣ז יָשִֽׁיר־מֹשֶׁה֩ וּבְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־הַשִּׁירָ֤ה הַזֹּאת֙ לַֽיהֹוָ֔ה
pairs.english: Then Moses and the children of Israel would sing [i.e., it entered their heart to sing] this song to the L-rd,
and they said: I shall sing to the L-rd
for He is exalted [over all the] exalted: horse and its rider [joined together] He cast into the sea.
The strength and vengeance of the L-rd has been salvation to me. This is my G-d [(His glory was so manifest that they pointed to it)]
and I will extol Him; the G-d of my father [(Not I, but my forefathers are the origin of this hallowing)], and I will exalt Him.
The L-rd is the Master of war;
the L-rd is His name [his "weapon," with which He wages war].
The chariots of Pharaoh and his host
He cast into the sea, and the élite of his officers were mired in the Red Sea, [the sea-bed turning into slime, measure for measure for their belaboring Israel with lime and bricks.]
[He mired them there] so that the waters should [return and] cover them;
they dropped to the depths like stone.
Your right hand, O L-rd,
is grand in power. Your right hand, O L-rd, breaks the foe.
And [if Your right hand, alone, breaks the foe, then, when it is uplifted] in the greatness of Your grandeur, [how much more so do]

You destroy those who rise up against You [i.e., those who rise up against Israel. And, if in the greatness of Your grandeur alone, they are destroyed, then,] when You send forth Your wrath, [how much more so] does it consume them as stubble!
And with the breath of Your nostrils [i.e., in the heat of Your anger],
the waters were [heated solid and] piled up. The waves stood up as a wall. The depths were congealed [into stone, and the Egyptians were dashed against it] in the fury of the sea.
The foe (i.e., Pharaoh) said [to his people in urging them to pursue Israel:]
I shall pursue, I shall overtake, I shall divide (the) spoil [with my officers and servants].
My spirit [i.e., my desire] will be filled with them. I shall draw forth my sword; my hand will impoverish them.
You blew with Your breath —
the sea covered them; they plummeted like lead in the mighty waters.
Who is like You among the mighty,
O L-rd? Who is like You, majestic in holiness, dreaded in praise [i.e., men dreading to praise You lest they fall short in Your praises], doing wonders!
You inclined Your right hand [and they fell — all being contained in Your hand] —
the earth swallowed them up [(whence it is derived that they merited burial for vindicating G-d's judgment upon them)].
You have led forth in Your kindness
this people whom You have redeemed. You have guided them in Your strength to Your holy habitation.
Peoples heard —

they tremble; quaking has seized the inhabitants of Plasheth [(for having killed the sons of Ephraim, who "pushed" the redemption prematurely and were killed by the inhabitants of Gath (I Chronicles 7:21)].
Then the chiefs of
Edom were confounded; the mighty ones of Moav were seized
with trembling. [Even though they were not the "target," they were mortified by Israel's ascendancy]; all the inhabitants of Canaan melted [in fear of destruction and conquest].
There fell upon them dread [(upon the distant — see Joshua 2:9-10)]
and terror [(upon the near)]; by the greatness of Your arm they will be (struck) still
as stone. Until Your people, O L-rd, pass over [the Arnon]; until there pass over [the Jordan] this people, O L-rd, whom You have acquired [endearingly] (to Yourself).
You will bring them and You will plant them [("them" and not "us" — Moses prophesying in effect that he himself would not enter the land)]
in the mountain of Your inheritance, aligned with Your habitation [the Throne of Glory], which You have made,

O L-rd — the sanctuary, O L-rd, which Your [two] hands have established [(the sanctuary being more beloved of the L-rd than the world, which He created with one hand (Psalms 48:13). And when will it be rebuilt with two hands? At that time when… (18)]
the L-rd will reign
for ever and ever.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י בָא֩ ס֨וּס פַּרְעֹ֜ה בְּרִכְבּ֤וֹ וּבְפָרָשָׁיו֙
pairs.english: When the horse of Pharaoh came with its chariot and its riders

pairs.hebrew: בַּיָּ֔ם        וַיָּ֧שֶׁב יְהֹוָ֛ה עֲלֵהֶ֖ם אֶת־מֵ֣י הַיָּ֑ם        וּבְנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הָלְכ֥וּ בַיַּבָּשָׁ֖ה בְּת֥וֹךְ הַיָּֽם׃ {פ}
pairs.english: into the sea, and the L-rd turned back upon them the waters of the sea, and the children of Israel walked on the dry land in the midst of the sea —

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּקַּח֩ מִרְיָ֨ם הַנְּבִיאָ֜ה אֲח֧וֹת אַהֲרֹ֛ן אֶת־הַתֹּ֖ף בְּיָדָ֑הּ
pairs.english: Then Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron [(Miriam having prophesied the birth of Moses, etc., while she was only the sister of Aaron)] took the timbrel in her hand [(the righteous women of that generation having taken timbrels out of Egypt in their certitude that G-d would work miracles for Israel)],
and all the women went out after her with timbrels and dances.
And Miriam answered to them [(Moses chanted to the men, and they responded after him, and Miriam chanted to the women (1):]
"Sing to the L-rd, for He is exalted [over all the] exalted;
horse and its rider He cast into the sea."

And Moses made Israel journey from the Red Sea [against their wills (the Egyptians having adorned their horses with gold, silver, and precious stones, which the Israelites lingered to collect, "the spoils of the sea" exceeding the spoils of Egypt)],
and Israel went out to the desert of Shur,
and they traveled three days in the desert without finding any water.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ מָרָ֔תָה וְלֹ֣א יָֽכְל֗וּ לִשְׁתֹּ֥ת מַ֙יִם֙ מִמָּרָ֔ה
pairs.english: And they came to Marah, and they could not drink the waters of Marah,
for they were bitter (marim) —
wherefore it is called Marah.
And the people caviled against Moses, saying:
"What shall we drink!"
And he cried out to the L-rd, and the L-rd showed him a tree;
and he cast it into the waters and the waters were sweetened.
There He made for them statute and judgment [(He gave them for study some of the areas of Torah — Sabbath, the red heifer, jurisdiction)],
and there He tried them [(and "discovered" their stiff-neckedness, their not imploring Moses, but caviling against him)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֩אמֶר֩ אִם־שָׁמ֨וֹעַ תִּשְׁמַ֜ע לְק֣וֹל ׀ יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ
pairs.english: And He said: If you pay heed to the voice of the L-rd your G-d, [taking upon yourselves to perform the mitzvoth],

pairs.hebrew: וְהַיָּשָׁ֤ר בְּעֵינָיו֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה וְהַֽאֲזַנְתָּ֙ לְמִצְוֺתָ֔יו וְשָׁמַרְתָּ֖ כׇּל־חֻקָּ֑יו
pairs.english: and you do what is just in His eyes, [performing them], and you give ear to His mitzvoth, [being attentive to their details], and you keep all of His statutes, [decrees having no ostensible reason, and, therefore, "vulnerable to attack" by the evil inclination (e.g., the prohibitions against wearing kilaim and eating swine, the institution of the red heifer, and the like)] —
then [if you observe My mitzvoth], all of the illness which I placed upon Egypt I will not place upon you,
for I am the L-rd who heals you [by "prescribing" (Torah and mitzvoth) against this illness].
And they came to Eilim,

pairs.hebrew: וְשָׁ֗ם שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֛ה עֵינֹ֥ת מַ֖יִם וְשִׁבְעִ֣ים תְּמָרִ֑ים
pairs.english: and there (they found) twelve springs of water, [for each of the twelve tribes], and seventy palm trees, [for each of the seventy elders],
and they encamped there by the waters.
And they journeyed from Eilim,

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ כׇּל־עֲדַ֤ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־מִדְבַּר־סִ֔ין אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֵּין־אֵילִ֖ם וּבֵ֣ין סִינָ֑י
pairs.english: and the entire congregation of the children of Israel came to the desert of Sin between Eilim and Sinai

pairs.hebrew: בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֨ה עָשָׂ֥ר יוֹם֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י לְצֵאתָ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: on the fifteenth day of the second month of their going out from the land of Egypt [(whence we derive that of the left-over dough they ate sixty-one meals, and the manna descended for them on the sixteenth of Iyyar)].
And the entire congregation of the children of Israel caviled
against Moses and Aaron in the desert [because their bread had ended].
And the children of Israel said to them:
Would that we had died by the hand of the L-rd in the land of Egypt,

pairs.hebrew: בְּשִׁבְתֵּ֙נוּ֙ עַל־סִ֣יר הַבָּשָׂ֔ר בְּאׇכְלֵ֥נוּ לֶ֖חֶם לָשֹׂ֑בַע
pairs.english: when we sat over the fleshpot, when we ate bread to satiety!

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־הוֹצֵאתֶ֤ם אֹתָ֙נוּ֙ אֶל־הַמִּדְבָּ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה לְהָמִ֛ית אֶת־כׇּל־הַקָּהָ֥ל הַזֶּ֖ה בָּרָעָֽב׃ {ס}
pairs.english: For you have taken us out to this desert to kill this entire congregation by famine!

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה הִנְנִ֨י מַמְטִ֥יר לָכֶ֛ם לֶ֖חֶם מִן־הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Behold, I shall rain down bread for you from heaven,
and the people shall go out and gather each day's ration in its day, [and not one day for another],
so that I may try them, whether or not they will walk in My law [(not to leave over of it until morning and not to go out to gather on Shabbath)].

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁ֔י וְהֵכִ֖ינוּ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־יָבִ֑יאוּ
pairs.english: And it shall be, on the sixth day, that they shall prepare what they shall bring,
and it shall be [after they have gathered it] double [(for Friday and Shabbath)] what they gather every day.
And Moses and Aaron said to all the children of Israel:

pairs.hebrew: עֶ֕רֶב וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֧י יְהֹוָ֛ה הוֹצִ֥יא אֶתְכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: In the evening [when He sends out the quail], you will know that the L-rd [and not we (3)] took you out of the land of Egypt.

And in the morning [when you receive the manna], you will see the glory [i.e., the beneficence] of the L-rd, [the manna being given with a "radiant countenance" (the request for bread being "legitimate") as opposed to the quail, which was given "grudgingly"],
for He hears your cavilings, [which are] against the L-rd.
And we, [of] what [significance] are we that you cause [(everyone) your families and your mixed multitude] to cavil against us?

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה בְּתֵ֣ת יְהֹוָה֩ לָכֶ֨ם בָּעֶ֜רֶב בָּשָׂ֣ר לֶאֱכֹ֗ל וְלֶ֤חֶם בַּבֹּ֙קֶר֙ לִשְׂבֹּ֔עַ
pairs.english: And Moses said: (You will see this) when the L-rd gives to you in the evening flesh to eat, and bread in the morning to satiety [(but not flesh to satiety — whence we infer that flesh is not to be eaten to satiety)],

pairs.hebrew: בִּשְׁמֹ֤עַ יְהֹוָה֙ אֶת־תְּלֻנֹּ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־אַתֶּ֥ם מַלִּינִ֖ם עָלָ֑יו
pairs.english: for the L-rd hears your cavilings whereby you cause [others] to cavil against Him.

pairs.hebrew: וְנַ֣חְנוּ מָ֔ה לֹא־עָלֵ֥ינוּ תְלֻנֹּתֵיכֶ֖ם כִּ֥י עַל־יְהֹוָֽה׃
pairs.english: And what are we? Not against us are your cavilings, but against the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֔ן אֱמֹ֗ר אֶֽל־כׇּל־עֲדַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל
pairs.english: And Moses said to Aaron: Say to the entire congregation of the children of Israel:
Draw near before the L-rd [to the place where the clouds will descend],
for He has heard your cavilings.
And it was, as Aaron spoke to the entire congregation of the children of Israel,
that they turned to the desert,
and, behold, the glory of the L-rd appeared in the cloud.
And the L-rd spoke to Moses,
saying:

pairs.hebrew: שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי אֶת־תְּלוּנֹּת֮ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ דַּבֵּ֨ר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר
pairs.english: I have heard the cavilings of the children of Israel. Speak to them, saying:

pairs.hebrew: בֵּ֤ין הָֽעַרְבַּ֙יִם֙ תֹּאכְל֣וּ בָשָׂ֔ר וּבַבֹּ֖קֶר תִּשְׂבְּעוּ־לָ֑חֶם
pairs.english: Towards evening you will eat flesh, and in the morning you will be sated with bread;
and you will know that I am the L-rd your G-d.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֣י בָעֶ֔רֶב וַתַּ֣עַל הַשְּׂלָ֔ו וַתְּכַ֖ס אֶת־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה
pairs.english: And it was in the evening that the quail arose and covered the camp,

pairs.hebrew: וּבַבֹּ֗קֶר הָֽיְתָה֙ שִׁכְבַ֣ת הַטַּ֔ל סָבִ֖יב לַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃
pairs.english: and in the morning there was a layer of dew [covering the manna] around the camp, [the manna being "sandwiched" in dew (see Numbers 11:9)].
And the dew layer ascended [when the sun rose],

pairs.hebrew: וְהִנֵּ֞ה עַל־פְּנֵ֤י הַמִּדְבָּר֙ דַּ֣ק מְחֻסְפָּ֔ס דַּ֥ק כַּכְּפֹ֖ר עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
pairs.english: and, behold, on the face of the desert, thin [i.e., a thin thing] was revealed [spread] thin as hoarfrost upon the ground.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּרְא֣וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ אִ֤ישׁ אֶל־אָחִיו֙ מָ֣ן ה֔וּא
pairs.english: And the children of Israel saw it, and each said to his neighbor: "It is man" [(a food) "preparation"],
for they did not know what it was [to call it by its name.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם ה֣וּא הַלֶּ֔חֶם אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֧ן יְהֹוָ֛ה לָכֶ֖ם לְאׇכְלָֽה׃
pairs.english: And Moses said to them: This is the bread that the L-rd has given to you to eat.
This is the thing that the L-rd has commanded:
Gather of it each man according to his eating,

pairs.hebrew: עֹ֣מֶר לַגֻּלְגֹּ֗לֶת מִסְפַּר֙ נַפְשֹׁ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם אִ֛ישׁ לַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּאׇהֳל֖וֹ תִּקָּֽחוּ׃
pairs.english: an omer [(a certain measure)] for a head [according to] the number of your souls [in your tent]; each for [the number] in his tent shall you take.
And the children of Israel did so,
and they gathered, some (taking) more [than an omer for a head], some less.
[But when they came home] and they measured it in the omer (a measuring vessel of that size) [they found that]

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹ֤א הֶעְדִּיף֙ הַמַּרְבֶּ֔ה וְהַמַּמְעִ֖יט לֹ֣א הֶחְסִ֑יר
pairs.english: he who had taken more did not exceed [the omer] and he who had taken less did not diminish;
each according to his eating had they gathered.
And Moses said to them:
Let no man leave over of it until morning.

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹא־שָׁמְע֣וּ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיּוֹתִ֨רוּ אֲנָשִׁ֤ים מִמֶּ֙נּוּ֙ עַד־בֹּ֔קֶר
pairs.english: And they did not heed Moses, and men [Dathan and Aviram] left over of it until morning,
and it was rotted and raised worms,
and Moses was wroth with them.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּלְקְט֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ בַּבֹּ֣קֶר בַּבֹּ֔קֶר אִ֖ישׁ כְּפִ֣י אׇכְל֑וֹ
pairs.english: And they gathered it each morning, each according to his eating;
and when the sun was hot (i.e., strong), it [that which remained in the field] melted.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֣י ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁ֗י לָֽקְט֥וּ לֶ֙חֶם֙ מִשְׁנֶ֔ה שְׁנֵ֥י הָעֹ֖מֶר לָאֶחָ֑ד
pairs.english: And it was, on the sixth day, they [found that they had] gathered double bread, two omers for [each] one.

And all the princes of the congregation came and they told it to Moses [(who had not commanded them as he had been told (5), for which reason he was included in (28): "How long will you refuse to keep My mitzvoth and My laws?")]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם ה֚וּא אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהֹוָ֔ה
pairs.english: And he said to them: This is what the L-rd had spoken:
A resting, a holy Sabbath is it to the L-rd tomorrow.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־תֹּאפ֞וּ אֵפ֗וּ וְאֵ֤ת אֲשֶֽׁר־תְּבַשְּׁלוּ֙ בַּשֵּׁ֔לוּ
pairs.english: What you bake [in an oven] (of the manna)] bake [all of it today for two days], and what you would cook [in water] cook;

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵת֙ כׇּל־הָ֣עֹדֵ֔ף הַנִּ֧יחוּ לָכֶ֛ם לְמִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת עַד־הַבֹּֽקֶר׃
pairs.english: and all the rest put by for yourselves in keeping until the morning.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּנִּ֤יחוּ אֹתוֹ֙ עַד־הַבֹּ֔קֶר כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֣ה מֹשֶׁ֑ה
pairs.english: And they put it by until the morning, as the L-rd had commanded Moses,
and it did not rot, and there was no worm in it.

[In the morning, when they were wont to go out and gather the manna, they came and asked Moses: "Shall we go out or not?"] And Moses said: Eat it [(what you have)] today. [They returned towards evening and asked: "Shall we go out now?" He answered that they should not]
for it is Sabbath today to the L-rd. [Seeing them to be worried that the manna might not fall again, he said:]
Today you will not find it in the field, [but tomorrow you will.]
Six days you shall gather it,
and on the seventh day it is Sabbath; there will not be [manna] on it, [Scripture hereby including Yom Kippur and festivals (as days on which manna does not fall)].

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְהִי֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י יָצְא֥וּ מִן־הָעָ֖ם לִלְקֹ֑ט
pairs.english: And it was on the seventh day that some of the people went out to gather,
and they did not find.
And the L-rd said to Moses [("The cabbage is smitten with the thorn" — see 22)]:
How long will you refuse to keep My mitzvoth and My laws?
See [with your own eyes] that the L-rd has given you the Sabbath [to be observed],

pairs.hebrew: עַל־כֵּ֠ן ה֣וּא נֹתֵ֥ן לָכֶ֛ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁ֖י לֶ֣חֶם יוֹמָ֑יִם
pairs.english: wherefore He gives you on the sixth day bread for two days.

pairs.hebrew: שְׁב֣וּ ׀ אִ֣ישׁ תַּחְתָּ֗יו אַל־יֵ֥צֵא אִ֛ישׁ מִמְּקֹמ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִֽי׃
pairs.english: Let each man sit in his place; let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.
And the people rested
on the seventh day.
And the children of Israel called its name "man" (see 15).
And it was [round] like coriander seed and [(unlike coriander seed)] white,
and its taste was like dough fried in honey.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה זֶ֤ה הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה יְהֹוָ֔ה
pairs.english: And Moses said: This is the thing that the L-rd commanded:
Fill the omer with it as a keeping for your generations,

pairs.hebrew: לְמַ֣עַן ׀ יִרְא֣וּ אֶת־הַלֶּ֗חֶם אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֶאֱכַ֤לְתִּי אֶתְכֶם֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר בְּהוֹצִיאִ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: so that they see the bread that I fed you in the desert when I took you out of the land of Egypt.
And Moses said to Aaron [(when the tent of meeting had been erected)]:

pairs.hebrew: קַ֚ח צִנְצֶ֣נֶת אַחַ֔ת וְתֶן־שָׁ֥מָּה מְלֹֽא־הָעֹ֖מֶר מָ֑ן
pairs.english: Take one earthen jug and put therein a full omer of manna

pairs.hebrew: וְהַנַּ֤ח אֹתוֹ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֔ה לְמִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶֽם׃
pairs.english: and place it before the L-rd [i.e., before the ark] as a keeping for your generations.
["And Moses said, etc." (above)] as the L-rd had commanded Moses.
And Aaron placed it before the [ark of] testimony for a keeping.

pairs.hebrew: וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָֽכְל֤וּ אֶת־הַמָּן֙ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה עַד־בֹּאָ֖ם אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ נוֹשָׁ֑בֶת
pairs.english: And the children of Israel ate the manna for forty years until they came to an inhabited land [on the other side of the Jordan (see Joshua 5:11-12)].

pairs.hebrew: אֶת־הַמָּן֙ אָֽכְל֔וּ עַד־בֹּאָ֕ם אֶל־קְצֵ֖ה אֶ֥רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃
pairs.english: They had eaten the manna [that had fallen on the seventh of Adar, (when Moses died, the manna ceasing with his death)], until they came to the edge of the land of Canaan [before they crossed the Jordan].
And the omer
is a tenth of an ephah [forty-three and one fifth eggs (the minimum amount for the separation of challah and for meal-offerings)].

pairs.hebrew: וַ֠יִּסְע֠וּ כׇּל־עֲדַ֨ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל מִמִּדְבַּר־סִ֛ין לְמַסְעֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־פִּ֣י יְהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: And the entire congregation of the children of Israel journeyed from the desert of Sin in their journeys by the word of the L-rd,
and they encamped in Refidim;
and there was no water to drink for the people.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֤רֶב הָעָם֙ עִם־מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ תְּנוּ־לָ֥נוּ מַ֖יִם וְנִשְׁתֶּ֑ה
pairs.english: And the people quarreled with Moses, and they said: Give us water and let us drink.
And Moses said to them: Why would you quarrel with me?
Why would you try the L-rd [to see if He can give water in a dry land]?

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּצְמָ֨א שָׁ֤ם הָעָם֙ לַמַּ֔יִם וַיָּ֥לֶן הָעָ֖ם עַל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה
pairs.english: And the people thirsted there for water, and the people caviled against Moses, and
said: Why did you bring us up from Egypt
to put to death me, my children, and my cattle by thirst?
And Moses cried out to the L-rd, saying:
What can I do to this people?
[If I wait] but a little more they will stone me!

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה עֲבֹר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Pass before the people [and see if they will stone you! (Why do you slander My children!)]
And take with you some of the elders of Israel [to attest that you are bringing forth the waters, that they were not there before].

pairs.hebrew: וּמַטְּךָ֗ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִכִּ֤יתָ בּוֹ֙ אֶת־הַיְאֹ֔ר קַ֥ח בְּיָדְךָ֖ וְהָלָֽכְתָּ׃
pairs.english: And your staff wherewith you smote the Nile take in your hand and go [that it not be said that it is a "punishment staff" (having been used against Pharaoh and Egypt, and that it cannot effect good)].
Behold, I shall stand before you there on the rock in Chorev,

pairs.hebrew: וְהִכִּ֣יתָ בַצּ֗וּר וְיָצְא֥וּ מִמֶּ֛נּוּ מַ֖יִם וְשָׁתָ֣ה הָעָ֑ם
pairs.english: and you shall strike in the rock [into it, the staff being of hard sapphire] and water will come out of it and the people will drink.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ כֵּן֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י זִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
pairs.english: And Moses did thus before the eyes of the elders of Israel.
And he called the name of the place Massah and Merivah

pairs.hebrew: עַל־רִ֣יב ׀ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְעַ֨ל נַסֹּתָ֤ם אֶת־יְהֹוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר
pairs.english: because of the "quarrel" (riv) of the children of Israel and because of their "proving" (nasotham) the L-rd, saying:
"Is the L-rd in our midst or not?"
And Amalek came
and warred with Israel in Refidim [(the Holy One Blessed be He saying, as it were: After everything, you have the temerity to ask if I am in your midst? I shall "sic the dog (Amalek)" upon you!)]

And Moses said to Joshua: Choose for us [you and me (whence it is derived that the honor of one's disciple should be as dear to one as his own)] men [warriors and fearers of sin, whose merits will avail them]
and go out [of the cloud] and do battle with Amalek.

pairs.hebrew: מָחָ֗ר אָנֹכִ֤י נִצָּב֙ עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הַגִּבְעָ֔ה וּמַטֵּ֥ה הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּיָדִֽי׃
pairs.english: Tomorrow I shall stand upon the top of the hill with the staff of G-d in my hand.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר אָֽמַר־לוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם בַּעֲמָלֵ֑ק
pairs.english: And Joshua did as Moses said to him, to war against Amalek.

pairs.hebrew: וּמֹשֶׁה֙ אַהֲרֹ֣ן וְח֔וּר עָל֖וּ רֹ֥אשׁ הַגִּבְעָֽה׃
pairs.english: And Moses, Aaron, and Chur [the son of Miriam and Calev] went up to the top of the hill [(whence it is derived that three must officiate (in prayer) on a fast day (Israel fasting at that time)].

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָ֗ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרִ֥ים מֹשֶׁ֛ה יָד֖וֹ וְגָבַ֣ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: And it was, when Moses lifted his hand, that Israel prevailed,
and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed. ["Now is it the hands of Moses that gain the victory!, etc." (see Rosh Hashanah 29a)]
And the hands of Moses became heavy [because he was lax in the mitzvah and deputed it to another (Joshua)],
and they [Aaron and Chur] took a stone [(but not a pillow)] and placed it beneath him [(Moses associating himself with Israel's suffering)], and he sat on it.

pairs.hebrew: וְאַהֲרֹ֨ן וְח֜וּר תָּֽמְכ֣וּ בְיָדָ֗יו מִזֶּ֤ה אֶחָד֙ וּמִזֶּ֣ה אֶחָ֔ד
pairs.english: And Aaron and Chur supported his hands — one on one side, one on the other.

And he was [i.e., he persisted with] his hands [spread out in an attitude of] steadfastness [in prayer] until the sun set. [The Amalekites would determine "propitious hours" for victory astrologically, and Moses caused the sun to stand still, thus confounding their reckonings.]
And Joshua weakened Amalek and his people
with the sword [(He decapitated their warriors and left only the weaker ones (whence we infer that he wrought by Divine command)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה כְּתֹ֨ב זֹ֤את זִכָּרוֹן֙ בַּסֵּ֔פֶר
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Write this as a remembrance in the book [(that Amalek initiated war with Israel before all other nations],

and place it in the ears of Joshua [who will bring Israel into the land, that he command Israel to give Amalek his due recompense (a hint to Moses that Joshua and not he will bring them into Eretz Yisrael)]

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־מָחֹ֤ה אֶמְחֶה֙ אֶת־זֵ֣כֶר עֲמָלֵ֔ק מִתַּ֖חַת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: because I desire to blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under the heavens, [for which reason I exhort you thus].
And Moses built an altar
and he called its name "The L-rd is my miracle."
And he said: For [the] hand [of the L-rd is raised to swear] by the throne [kes (as opposed to the complete form, kissei)] of Kah (the L-rd) [(as opposed to the complete name, Yod-Keh-Vav-Keh)]:
"The L-rd is at war with Amalek from generation to generation" [The import: G-d's name will not be complete and His throne will not be complete until the name of Amalek is blotted out.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁמַ֞ע יִתְר֨וֹ כֹהֵ֤ן מִדְיָן֙ חֹתֵ֣ן מֹשֶׁ֔ה
pairs.english: And Yithro heard [(of the splitting of the Red Sea and the war with Amalek and he came to join Israel)], the chief of Midian, the father-in-law of Moses [(Yithro now priding himself in Moses, whereas previously the reverse was the case (see 4:18)],

pairs.hebrew: אֵת֩ כׇּל־אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ לְמֹשֶׁ֔ה וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַמּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: all that G-d had done [(the falling of the manna, the welling of the water, the defeat of Amalek)] with Moses and with Israel, His people [(Moses being equated with all of Israel)] —
that the L-rd had taken Israel out of Egypt [(this being the greatest of all)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֗ח יִתְרוֹ֙ חֹתֵ֣ן מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶת־צִפֹּרָ֖ה אֵ֣שֶׁת מֹשֶׁ֑ה
pairs.english: And Yithro, Moses' father-in-law took Tzipporah, Moses' wife,
after she had been sent [back to her father's house to spare her suffering in Egypt].
And her two sons,
the name of the first, Gershom;

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י אָמַ֔ר גֵּ֣ר הָיִ֔יתִי בְּאֶ֖רֶץ נׇכְרִיָּֽה׃
pairs.english: for he (Moses) said: "I was a stranger (ger) in a foreign land,"
And the name of the second, Eliezer,
for (he said): "The G-d of (Elokei) my father was my help (be'ezri),
and He saved me from the sword of Pharaoh" [When Dathan and Aviram exposed Moses (see 2:14-15) and Pharaoh ordered him decapitated, his neck became a pillar of marble.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֞א יִתְר֨וֹ חֹתֵ֥ן מֹשֶׁ֛ה וּבָנָ֥יו וְאִשְׁתּ֖וֹ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה
pairs.english: And Yithro, Moses' father-in-law, and his sons and his wife came to Moses

pairs.hebrew: אֶל־הַמִּדְבָּ֗ר אֲשֶׁר־ה֛וּא חֹנֶ֥ה שָׁ֖ם הַ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃
pairs.english: to the desert [(a tribute to Yithro, his leaving magnificence for the desert)], where he was encamped, (to the) mountain of G-d.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֲנִ֛י חֹתֶנְךָ֥ יִתְר֖וֹ בָּ֣א אֵלֶ֑יךָ
pairs.english: And he said to Moses: I, your father-in-law, Yithro, am coming to you;
and your wife and her two sons with her. [If you do not come out for my sake, come out for your wife's sake, and if not for her sake, for your sons' sake.]
And Moses went out to his father-in-law, [followed by Aaron, Nadav and Avihu, all who saw them following in their wake — a monumental show of honor to Yithro]
and he [Moses] bowed down to him and kissed him, and they greeted each other,
and they came into the tent.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְסַפֵּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ לְחֹ֣תְנ֔וֹ אֵת֩ כׇּל־אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֤ה יְהֹוָה֙ לְפַרְעֹ֣ה וּלְמִצְרַ֔יִם עַ֖ל אוֹדֹ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: And Moses related to his father-in-law [(to appeal to his feelings, to draw him to Torah)] all that the L-rd did to Pharaoh and to Egypt on behalf of Israel,
all the ordeals [(at the Red Sea and with Amalek)] that they had undergone upon the way
and how the L-rd had rescued them.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּ֣חַדְּ יִתְר֔וֹ עַ֚ל כׇּל־הַטּוֹבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֥ה יְהֹוָ֖ה לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: And Yithro rejoiced over all the good that the L-rd had done to Israel [the manna, the well, the Torah, and, above all,]
His rescuing them from the hand of Egypt. [Until now, one slave could not escape from Egypt — and now, six hundred thousand!]
And Yithro said: Blessed is the L-rd,

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִצִּ֥יל אֶתְכֶ֛ם מִיַּ֥ד מִצְרַ֖יִם וּמִיַּ֣ד פַּרְעֹ֑ה
pairs.english: who rescued you from the hand of Egypt [a hard people] and from the hand of Pharaoh [a hard king],
who rescued the people from under the [oppressive] hand of Egypt.
Now I know [even more than in the past] that greater is the L-rd than all the gods [(There was no idolatry in the world that Yithro had not served)].
For [they (the Egyptians) were destroyed] by the [very] thing [water] whereby they devised evil against them.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֞ח יִתְר֨וֹ חֹתֵ֥ן מֹשֶׁ֛ה עֹלָ֥ה וּזְבָחִ֖ים לֵֽאלֹהִ֑ים
pairs.english: And Yithro, Moses' father-in-law, took a burnt-offering and peace-offerings (for sacrifice) to G-d.
And Aaron and all the elders of Israel [(with Moses "in attendance")] came
to eat bread with Moses' father-in-law before G-d [(whence it is seen that deriving enjoyment from a feast partaken of by Torah scholars is akin to basking in the Divine radiance)].

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִֽמׇּחֳרָ֔ת וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב מֹשֶׁ֖ה לִשְׁפֹּ֣ט אֶת־הָעָ֑ם
pairs.english: And it was [on the day after Yom Kippur] on the morrow [of Moses' descent from the mountain with the second tablets (This section is out of chronological order)] that Moses sat [like a king] to judge the people,

and the people stood, (waiting) upon Moses from morning to evening ["Every judge who judges a true judgment in its (essential) truth, even for one moment, Scripture accounts it to him as if he had occupied himself with Torah the entire day ('from morning to evening') and as if he were a partner with the Holy One Blessed be He in the creation" (see Genesis 1:5)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּרְא֙ חֹתֵ֣ן מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֵ֛ת כׇּל־אֲשֶׁר־ה֥וּא עֹשֶׂ֖ה לָעָ֑ם
pairs.english: And Moses' father-in-law saw all that he did to the people,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מָֽה־הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַתָּ֤ה עֹשֶׂה֙ לָעָ֔ם
pairs.english: and he said: What is this thing that you do to the people?

pairs.hebrew: מַדּ֗וּעַ אַתָּ֤ה יוֹשֵׁב֙ לְבַדֶּ֔ךָ וְכׇל־הָעָ֛ם נִצָּ֥ב עָלֶ֖יךָ מִן־בֹּ֥קֶר עַד־עָֽרֶב׃
pairs.english: Why do you sit by yourself and all the people wait upon you from morning to evening?
And Moses said to his father-in-law:
Because the people come to me to enquire [(concerning the law)] of G-d.
When they have a matter [to be resolved], he [the one who "has the matter"] comes to me,
and I judge between a man and his neighbor,
and I make known the statutes of G-d and His laws.
And the father-in-law of Moses [(Scripture honoring Yithro by this appellation)] said to him:
The thing that you do is not good.

pairs.hebrew: נָבֹ֣ל תִּבֹּ֔ל גַּם־אַתָּ֕ה גַּם־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמָּ֑ךְ
pairs.english: You will languish, both you [including Aaron and Chur and the seventy elders] and this people that is with you.

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־כָבֵ֤ד מִמְּךָ֙ הַדָּבָ֔ר לֹא־תוּכַ֥ל עֲשֹׂ֖הוּ לְבַדֶּֽךָ׃
pairs.english: For this thing is beyond your strength; you will not be able to do it alone.

pairs.hebrew: עַתָּ֞ה שְׁמַ֤ע בְּקֹלִי֙ אִיעָ֣צְךָ֔ וִיהִ֥י אֱלֹהִ֖ים עִמָּ֑ךְ
pairs.english: Now, hearken to my voice. I shall counsel you, and let G-d be with you [in counsel; consult Him on this].
You be to the people [an intermediary] to G-d, [receiving judgment from Him],
and you bring the matters [i.e., their disputes] to G-d.
And you shall exhort them in respect to the statutes and the Toroth;

pairs.hebrew: וְהוֹדַעְתָּ֣ לָהֶ֗ם אֶת־הַדֶּ֙רֶךְ֙ יֵ֣לְכוּ בָ֔הּ וְאֶת־הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲשֽׂוּן׃
pairs.english: and you shall apprise them of the way in which they shall go, and of the deed that they shall do.

pairs.hebrew: וְאַתָּ֣ה תֶחֱזֶ֣ה מִכׇּל־הָ֠עָ֠ם אַנְשֵׁי־חַ֜יִל יִרְאֵ֧י אֱלֹהִ֛ים אַנְשֵׁ֥י אֱמֶ֖ת שֹׂ֣נְאֵי בָ֑צַע
pairs.english: And you shall see from all the people [through the holy spirit that is upon you] men of valor [rich men, who need not toady to anyone], fearers of G-d, trustworthy men, haters of gain [at the expense of integrity];

pairs.hebrew: וְשַׂמְתָּ֣ עֲלֵהֶ֗ם שָׂרֵ֤י אֲלָפִים֙ שָׂרֵ֣י מֵא֔וֹת
pairs.english: and (from these) place over them (the people) officers of thousands [600 officers for 600,000]; officers of hundreds, [6,000];
officers of fifties [12,000]; and officers of tens [60,000].
And they shall judge the people at all times.
And it shall be, every major thing shall they bring to you,
and every minor thing shall they themselves judge,
and it shall be easier for you, and they shall bear (the burden) with you.

pairs.hebrew: אִ֣ם אֶת־הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה וְצִוְּךָ֣ אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְיָֽכׇלְתָּ֖ עֲמֹ֑ד
pairs.english: If you do this thing and G-d will command you [to do it], then you will be able to bear up [(but not if He does not command you to do it)];

pairs.hebrew: וְגַם֙ כׇּל־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה עַל־מְקֹמ֖וֹ יָבֹ֥א בְשָׁלֽוֹם׃
pairs.english: and also all of this people [Aaron, Nadav, Avihu, and the seventy elders who are with you] shall come to their place in peace.
And Moses heeded his father-in-law's voice,
and he did all that he said.
And Moses chose men of valor from all of Israel,
and he made them heads of the people:

pairs.hebrew: שָׂרֵ֤י אֲלָפִים֙ שָׂרֵ֣י מֵא֔וֹת שָׂרֵ֥י חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים וְשָׂרֵ֥י עֲשָׂרֹֽת׃
pairs.english: officers of thousands, officers of hundreds, officers of fifties, and officers of tens.
And they judged the people at all times.
The hard thing they brought to Moses,
and the small thing they themselves judged.
And Moses sent his father-in-law
and he went to his land [to proselytize his family].

pairs.hebrew: בַּחֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י לְצֵ֥את בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם
pairs.english: On the third month of the exodus of the children of Israel from the land of Egypt,
on this day [on the New Moon ("Let words of Torah always be 'new' to you, as if they were given this day")], they came to the desert of Sinai.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּסְע֣וּ מֵרְפִידִ֗ים וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ מִדְבַּ֣ר סִינַ֔י וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר
pairs.english: And they journeyed from Refidim and they came to the desert of Sinai [(Just as they came to the desert of Sinai in a state of penitence, so they had left Refidim in a state of penitence.)]
And Israel encamped there ["as one man, with one heart"] opposite [i.e., east of] the mountain.
And Moses went up to G-d [early in the morning on the second day]
and the L-rd called to him from the mountain, saying:
Thus shall you say [(in this mode and in this order)] to the house of Jacob [the women (To them, "say" it, "gently")],
and speak (tagid) to the children of Israel [the men. (Lay down for them the things which are "tough as sinews" (giddin), the punishments and the details of the mitzvoth)].
You have seen [with your own eyes] what I did to Egypt [on your behalf],

and I bore you [(all of you in one day, from the places of your dispersion in the land of Goshen, to Ramses, assembling you for the Exodus)] on eagles' wings, [My angel protecting you from the projectiles of the foe (see 14:19-20), as an eagle, the highest flying of the birds, protects its young from other birds by carrying them on its wings],
and I brought you to Me.

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּ֗ה אִם־שָׁמ֤וֹעַ תִּשְׁמְעוּ֙ בְּקֹלִ֔י וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֑י
pairs.english: And now [(If you take it upon yourselves now, it will be "pleasant" for you in the future, all beginnings being difficult)], if you hearken to My voice and observe My covenant [that I shall make with you for the keeping of the Torah],
then you shall be unto Me a select treasure, above all the (other) peoples;
for all the earth [including the other peoples] is Mine, [(so that in choosing you it is clear that I am choosing you above them)].

pairs.hebrew: וְאַתֶּ֧ם תִּהְיוּ־לִ֛י מַמְלֶ֥כֶת כֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְג֣וֹי קָד֑וֹשׁ
pairs.english: And you shall be to Me a kingdom of lords and a holy nation.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֚לֶּה הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר תְּדַבֵּ֖ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
pairs.english: These are the words, [not less and not more] that you shall speak to the children of Israel.
And Moses came, and he called to the elders of the people,

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֣שֶׂם לִפְנֵיהֶ֗ם אֵ֚ת כׇּל־הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֖הוּ יְהֹוָֽה׃
pairs.english: and he put before them all these things that the L-rd had commanded him.
And all the people answered together and they said:
Whatever the L-rd has spoken we shall do.
And Moses [on the third day] returned the words of the people to the L-rd, [Moses doing what was "proper," though in no way "needed."]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י בָּ֣א אֵלֶ֘יךָ֮ בְּעַ֣ב הֶֽעָנָן֒
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Behold, I shall come to you in the thickness of the cloud

pairs.hebrew: בַּעֲב֞וּר יִשְׁמַ֤ע הָעָם֙ בְּדַבְּרִ֣י עִמָּ֔ךְ וְגַם־בְּךָ֖ יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ לְעוֹלָ֑ם
pairs.english: so that the people hear when I speak with you, and also in you [and in the prophets that follow you] they will believe forever.
And [on the fourth day] Moses told the words of the people [(to the effect that they wished to hear it from the King's own mouth)] to the L-rd.
And the L-rd said to Moses:
Go to the people and make them ready today and tomorrow,
and have them wash their garments.
And have them be ready for the third day [the sixth of Sivan (and on the fifth he erected the altar and the twelve monuments (see 24:4)],

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֗י יֵרֵ֧ד יְהֹוָ֛ה לְעֵינֵ֥י כׇל־הָעָ֖ם עַל־הַ֥ר סִינָֽי׃
pairs.english: for on the third day the L-rd will go down before the eyes of all the people [(the blind being cured)] on Mount Sinai.
And demarcate bounds for the people roundabout, [the bounds] "saying":

pairs.hebrew: הִשָּׁמְר֥וּ לָכֶ֛ם עֲל֥וֹת בָּהָ֖ר וּנְגֹ֣עַ בְּקָצֵ֑הוּ
pairs.english: Take heed unto yourselves not to go up on the mountain or to touch [even] its edge.
Whoever touches the mountain shall be put to death.

pairs.hebrew: לֹא־תִגַּ֨ע בּ֜וֹ יָ֗ד כִּֽי־סָק֤וֹל יִסָּקֵל֙ אוֹ־יָרֹ֣ה יִיָּרֶ֔ה
pairs.english: No hand shall touch it; for stoned shall he be stoned or cast down shall he be cast down [(whence it is derived that those executed by stoning are cast down from the stoning site, two (men's) statures high)].
Whether beast or man, he shall not live.
When the ram's horn sounds, [indicating the departure of the Shechinah], they may go up on the mountain.
And Moses went down [directly (not pausing for personal matters)] from the mountain to the people
and he made the people ready, and they washed their garments.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־הָעָ֔ם הֱי֥וּ נְכֹנִ֖ים לִשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֑ים
pairs.english: And he said to the people: Be ready in three days.
Do not draw near to a woman [for three days, (so that the woman can immerse on the third day and be ready (i.e., pure) to receive the Torah, ejected semen being "neutralized" by the third day)].
And it was, on the third day, when it was morning,

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִי֩ קֹלֹ֨ת וּבְרָקִ֜ים וְעָנָ֤ן כָּבֵד֙ עַל־הָהָ֔ר וְקֹ֥ל שֹׁפָ֖ר חָזָ֣ק מְאֹ֑ד
pairs.english: that there were thunders and lightnings, and a heavy cloud upon the mountain, and the sound of the shofar, very strong, [the Holy One Blessed be He preceding them — what flesh and blood would not do (the "Rabbi" waiting for His disciple!)],
and all the people in the camp trembled.

pairs.hebrew: וַיּוֹצֵ֨א מֹשֶׁ֧ה אֶת־הָעָ֛ם לִקְרַ֥את הָֽאֱלֹהִ֖ים מִן־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה
pairs.english: And Moses took out the people towards G-d, [(who was coming towards them, as a groom to a bride)] from the encampment,
and they stood at the foot of the mountain.

pairs.hebrew: וְהַ֤ר סִינַי֙ עָשַׁ֣ן כֻּלּ֔וֹ מִ֠פְּנֵ֠י אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרַ֥ד עָלָ֛יו יְהֹוָ֖ה בָּאֵ֑שׁ
pairs.english: And the whole of Mount Sinai smoked, for the L-rd had come down upon it in fire,
and its smoke rose like the smoke of a lime kiln,
and the whole mountain trembled greatly.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְהִי֙ ק֣וֹל הַשֹּׁפָ֔ר הוֹלֵ֖ךְ וְחָזֵ֣ק מְאֹ֑ד
pairs.english: And the sound of the shofar grew exceedingly strong [(the reverse of the normal phenomenon)].

When Moses spoke [the last eight commandments (after they had heard the first two from the L-rd Himself)], G-d answered him [i.e., acceded to his request] regarding the [amplification of his] voice, [so that he could be heard by the multitude].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֧רֶד יְהֹוָ֛ה עַל־הַ֥ר סִינַ֖י אֶל־רֹ֣אשׁ הָהָ֑ר
pairs.english: And the L-rd descended upon Mount Sinai [(He bent the heavens and spread them over the mountain, and the Throne of Glory descended upon them)] upon the top of the mountain.
And the L-rd called Moses to the top of the mountain,
and Moses went up.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה רֵ֖ד הָעֵ֣ד בָּעָ֑ם
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Go down and warn the people [(not to ascend the mountain)],
lest they break [their bounds in aspiring] to the L-rd to see, [and they draw near to the side of the mountain],
and there fall of them many, [(even the falling of one of them being regarded as the falling of "many")].
And also the priests [i.e., the first-born], who draw near to the L-rd [to offer sacrifices], let them [not ascend, but let them] be in readiness [to take their assigned stations],
lest the L-rd [kill them and] make a breach in them.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־יְהֹוָ֔ה לֹא־יוּכַ֣ל הָעָ֔ם לַעֲלֹ֖ת אֶל־הַ֣ר סִינָ֑י
pairs.english: And Moses said to the L-rd: The people will not be able to ascend Mount Sinai,

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־אַתָּ֞ה הַעֵדֹ֤תָה בָּ֙נוּ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַגְבֵּ֥ל אֶת־הָהָ֖ר וְקִדַּשְׁתּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: for You [already] warned us, saying: Demarcate bounds for the mountain and hallow it. [There is no need, then, for me to warn them again.]
And the L-rd said to him: Go, descend, [and warn them again, (prompting to zeal being called for both before the deed and at the time of the deed)],
and go up, you [in your precincts] and Aaron with you [in his precincts],

pairs.hebrew: וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְהָעָ֗ם אַל־יֶֽהֶרְס֛וּ לַעֲלֹ֥ת אֶל־יְהֹוָ֖ה פֶּן־יִפְרׇץ־בָּֽם׃
pairs.english: and the priests [in their precincts] — and the people, let them not break [their bounds at all] to ascend to the L-rd, lest He make a breach in them.
And Moses went down to the people
and he said (it) [this warning] to them.

And G-d [Elokim, the Judge, "exacting payment" (for all of the ten commandments, unlike some other sections in the Torah, where performance is rewarded, but non-performance not punished)] spoke all of these things [miraculously, in one utterance (after which He reiterated each commandment individually)]
saying, [i.e., the people responding in the affirmative or in the negative as per the nature of the commandment]:
I am the L-rd your G-d

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֧ר הוֹצֵאתִ֛יךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם מִבֵּ֣֥ית עֲבָדִ֑͏ֽים׃
pairs.english: who took you out of the land of Egypt [Having taken you out is sufficient reason that you be subservient to Me.] ("your [singular] G-d") [an opening for Moses to plead for Israel in the episode of the golden calf, viz.: "You said this ("your G-d") to me, not to them!"] from the house of [Pharaoh, to whom you were] servants.
There shall not be unto you [(You may not keep them even if you do not make them)] gods of [i.e., made by] others
before My presence [i.e., idolatry is interdicted not for this generation alone but eternally (just as I am eternally present)].
You shall not make for yourself a graven image or the likeness of anything
which is in the heavens above or in the earth below,
or in the waters beneath the earth.
You shall not bow down to them and you shall not serve them,

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י אָֽנֹכִ֞י יְהֹוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ אֵ֣ל קַנָּ֔א
pairs.english: for I am the L-rd your G-d, a jealous G-d, ["jealous" to exact punishment, and not "overlooking" idolatry],

pairs.hebrew: פֹּ֠קֵ֠ד עֲוֺ֨ן אָבֹ֧ת עַל־בָּנִ֛ים עַל־שִׁלֵּשִׁ֥ים וְעַל־רִבֵּעִ֖ים לְשֹׂנְאָֽ֑י׃
pairs.english: visiting the sins of the fathers upon the children, for the third and the fourth generations to those who hate Me, [those who perpetuate their fathers' ways],
And doing lovingkindness [i.e., "guarding" the lovingkindness that a man does, to reward him] for thousands [of generations],
for My lovers and the keepers of My mitzvoth, [whence (5 and 6) it is seen that G-d's "measure" of reward is greater than His measure for punishment].
You shall not take the name of the L-rd your G-d in vain [by swearing at variance with what is known, e.g., that a pillar of stone is one of gold],

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יְנַקֶּה֙ יְהֹוָ֔ה אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־יִשָּׂ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ לַשָּֽׁוְא׃ {פ}
pairs.english: for the L-rd will not absolve him who takes His name in vain.
Have [always] in remembrance the Sabbath day [("Remember" and "Keep" (Deuteronomy 5:12) were stated in one pronouncement)]
to set it apart [i.e., If you chance upon something specially fine, set it apart for the Sabbath].
Six days shall you work,
and you shall do all of your labor [i.e., When Shabbath arrives, let it be in your eyes as if all your labor has been done and give it no thought.]
And the seventh day is Sabbath to the L-rd your G-d.
You shall not perform any labor:

pairs.hebrew: אַתָּ֣ה ׀ וּבִנְךָ֣͏ֽ־וּ֠בִתֶּ֗ךָ עַבְדְּךָ֤֨ וַאֲמָֽתְךָ֜֙ וּבְהֶמְתֶּ֔֗ךָ וְגֵרְךָ֖֙ אֲשֶׁ֥֣ר בִּשְׁעָרֶֽ֔יךָ׃
pairs.english: you, and your son, and your daughter [minors — parents being exhorted vis-à-vis their young children], your man-servant, and your maid-servant, and your beast, and your sojourner in your gates.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י שֵֽׁשֶׁת־יָמִים֩ עָשָׂ֨ה יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם וְאֶת־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֶת־הַיָּם֙ וְאֶת־כׇּל־אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֔ם
pairs.english: For, six days did the L-rd make the heavens and the earth, the seas and all that is in them,
and He rested on the seventh day. [How much more so, then, must we — who feel toil — rest on that day!]
Therefore, the L-rd blessed the Sabbath day [by providing a double portion of manna on the sixth day], and He sanctified it [by not having the manna fall on the Sabbath].
Honor your father and your mother

pairs.hebrew: לְמַ֙עַן֙ יַאֲרִכ֣וּן יָמֶ֔יךָ עַ֚ל הָאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽךְ׃ {ס}
pairs.english: so that your days be prolonged on the earth that the L-rd your G-d gives to you, [the implication being that if you do not honor them your days will be shortened.]
You shall not
kill. You shall not commit adultery. You shall not steal [a human being, i.e., kidnap]. You shall not testify against your neighbor false testimony.
You shall not covet your neighbor's house. You shall not covet your neighbor's wife,

pairs.hebrew: וְעַבְדּ֤וֹ וַאֲמָתוֹ֙ וְשׁוֹר֣וֹ וַחֲמֹר֔וֹ וְכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְרֵעֶֽךָ׃ {פ}
pairs.english: and his man-servant, and his maid-servant, and his ox and his ass, and all that belongs to your neighbor.

pairs.hebrew: וְכׇל־הָעָם֩ רֹאִ֨ים אֶת־הַקּוֹלֹ֜ת וְאֶת־הַלַּפִּידִ֗ם וְאֵת֙ ק֣וֹל הַשֹּׁפָ֔ר וְאֶת־הָהָ֖ר עָשֵׁ֑ן
pairs.english: And all the people saw [(whence we derive that there were no blind ones among them)] ["saw" miraculously] the sounds [emanating from the Mighty One's mouth], and the lightnings, and the sound of the shofar, and the mountain smoking.
And the people saw and they shuddered,
and they stood far off. [(They recoiled twelve mil, the distance of their encampment, and ministering angels came and restored them)]
And they said to Moses: Speak, you with us, and we shall hear;
and let G-d not speak with us, lest we die.
And Moses said to the people: Do not fear,

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֗י לְבַֽעֲבוּר֙ נַסּ֣וֹת אֶתְכֶ֔ם בָּ֖א הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים
pairs.english: for to uplift you has G-d come

pairs.hebrew: וּבַעֲב֗וּר תִּהְיֶ֧ה יִרְאָת֛וֹ עַל־פְּנֵיכֶ֖ם לְבִלְתִּ֥י תֶחֱטָֽאוּ׃
pairs.english: and so that His fear [engendered by beholding His awe] be upon your faces, that you not sin.
And the people stood from afar,
and Moses drew near [within the three divisions: "darkness, cloud, and mist" (Deuteronomy 4:11)] to the mist [the "thickness of the cloud" (19:9)], where G-d was.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה כֹּ֥ה תֹאמַ֖ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Thus shall you say to the children of Israel:

pairs.hebrew: אַתֶּ֣ם רְאִיתֶ֔ם כִּ֚י מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי עִמָּכֶֽם׃
pairs.english: You saw [with your own eyes] that from the heavens I spoke to you ["to exhort you, and on the earth He showed you His great fire" (Deuteronomy 4:36)]
You shall not make [likenesses of those (the angels) who minister] unto Me.

pairs.hebrew: אֱלֹ֤הֵי כֶ֙סֶף֙ וֵאלֹהֵ֣י זָהָ֔ב לֹ֥א תַעֲשׂ֖וּ לָכֶֽם׃
pairs.english: Gods of silver [(If you make the cherubs who "stand with Me" of silver (instead of the prescribed gold), they will be considered "gods" (i.e., idols)], and gods of gold [(If you make more than two cherubs of gold, they will be considered "gods")], do not make for yourselves [i.e., in your synagogues and study halls, as I have bidden you make in the Temple].
An altar [fixed upon the] earth shall you make for Me, [i.e., in My name],

pairs.hebrew: וְזָבַחְתָּ֣ עָלָ֗יו אֶת־עֹלֹתֶ֙יךָ֙ וְאֶת־שְׁלָמֶ֔יךָ אֶת־צֹֽאנְךָ֖ וְאֶת־בְּקָרֶ֑ךָ
pairs.english: and you shall slaughter beside it your burnt-offerings and your peace-offerings, [which come from] your flocks and your herds.

pairs.hebrew: בְּכׇל־הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַזְכִּ֣יר אֶת־שְׁמִ֔י אָב֥וֹא אֵלֶ֖יךָ וּבֵרַכְתִּֽיךָ׃
pairs.english: Wherever I [permit you to] mention My name [i.e., in the Temple, where the Cohanim are authorized to utter the Ineffable Name in the priestly blessing], I shall come to you, [i.e., there shall I repose My shechinah] and I shall bless you.

pairs.hebrew: וְאִם־מִזְבַּ֤ח אֲבָנִים֙ תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־לִּ֔י לֹֽא־תִבְנֶ֥ה אֶתְהֶ֖ן גָּזִ֑ית
pairs.english: And when you make an altar of stones unto Me, do not build them hewn,
for if you lift your sword upon it, you profane it [(the altar being created to prolong life, and the sword, to shorten it)].
And do not go up by steps, [but by a smooth ramp] upon My altar,
so that your nakedness not be revealed upon it [by your having to take (relatively) long strides].

And these [(Just as what precedes was stated at Sinai, so these)] are the judgments [(this section being juxtaposed with that of the altar to teach that the Sanhedrin should preside near the sanctuary)]

that you should set [(as a "set" table, the judgments not merely to be mandated to them, but to be "digested" for them)] before them [and not before gentiles, even if their law, in the instance in question, coincides with Jewish law (this, to avoid diminution of the honor of Heaven)].
If you buy [from beth-din] a Hebrew man-servant,
six years shall he serve,
and in the seventh he shall go out to freedom, gratis.
If alone [without a wife] he came, alone shall he go out [(If he were not married when he came, his master may not give him a Canaanite bondswoman for the begetting of slaves)].

pairs.hebrew: אִם־בַּ֤עַל אִשָּׁה֙ ה֔וּא וְיָצְאָ֥ה אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ עִמּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: If he were the husband of a [Jewish] woman, then his wife shall go out with him. [(When did she come in?) It is hereby derived that one who buys a Hebrew man-servant is required to feed his wife and children.]

pairs.hebrew: אִם־אֲדֹנָיו֙ יִתֶּן־ל֣וֹ אִשָּׁ֔ה וְיָלְדָה־ל֥וֹ בָנִ֖ים א֣וֹ בָנ֑וֹת
pairs.english: If his master gives him a woman [a Canaanite bondswoman], and she bears him sons or daughters,
then the woman and her children shall belong to her master,
and he shall go out alone.
And if the man-servant will say:
I love my master, my wife [the bondswoman] and my children;
I shall not go out free,
then his master shall bring him near to the judges [(The man-servant must consult the judges who sold him)],
and he shall bring him near to the door or to the door-post [(Just as a door-post stands (in its place), so the door (against which his ear is bored) must be standing)],
and his master shall bore his [right] ear with an awl,

and he shall serve him forever [i.e., until the Jubilee year]. [Why the ear? The ear which heard on Mount Sinai: "Thou shalt not steal!" and he went and stole (for which reason beth-din sold him) — let his ear be bored! Or, if he sold himself: The ear which heard on Mount Sinai: "For unto Me are the children of Israel servants" and he went and acquired a master for himself — let his ear be bored! And why door and door-post? The Holy One Blessed be He said: The door and the door-post, which were witnesses in Egypt when I skipped over the lintel and the two door-posts (on which the Jews had sprinkled the blood of the Paschal lamb), and I said: "For unto Me are the children of Israel servants" — and not servants to servants (i.e., the Egyptians) and this one went and acquired a master for himself! Let his ear (that heard and did not listen) be bored (in their presence!)]
And if a man sells his daughter [a minor (under twelve)] as a maid,

she shall not go out as the [Canaanite] bondsmen go out, [with the master's knocking out a tooth or an eye (but: at the end of six years, at the Jubilee year, or at her bringing (pubertal) signs — whichever is first)].

pairs.hebrew: אִם־רָעָ֞ה בְּעֵינֵ֧י אֲדֹנֶ֛יהָ אֲשֶׁר־[ל֥וֹ] (לא) יְעָדָ֖הּ וְהֶפְדָּ֑הּ
pairs.english: If she be ill-favored in the eyes of her master, who [on that account] did not designate her [to be his wife, even though he should have], then he shall [help] redeem her [by deducting from her six-year redemption money the value of the service she had already rendered].

To a strange nation [i.e., to another man] he [both the master and the father] shall not presume to sell her, after he [the master, by not taking her to wife, or the father, by selling her] has been faithless to her.
And if [as is the master's prerogative,] to his son he designate her, [(the purchase money serving as the betrothal money)],
according to the ordinance of the daughters ["her food, her clothing, and her (conjugal) time" (10)] shall he provide for her.
If another (wife) he take for himself [in addition to her],
her [the first one's] food, her clothing, and her (conjugal) time he shall not diminish.
And if [one of] these three [viz. marrying her himself, marrying her to his son, or deducting from her redemption money] he does not do to her,
then she shall go out gratis, without money [(Scripture providing an additional way for her to go out, viz., showing signs of puberty)].
If one strikes a man [(only one who is destined to be a "man," and not a fetus that is certain to die of itself)], and he dies,
then, [i.e., only if it is a death-dealing blow], he shall be put to death.

pairs.hebrew: וַאֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א צָדָ֔ה וְהָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אִנָּ֣ה לְיָד֑וֹ
pairs.english: And if he did not lie in wait (for him), but G-d put (him) into his hand,
then I shall make for you a place [even (now) in the desert] where he shall flee, [that place being the Levite encampment.]

And if a man be deliberate, [and not unwitting] against his neighbor, [and not against a gentile], to kill him with subtlety [(to exclude a doctor whose patient dies as a result of his treatment, a bailiff of beth-din who kills in the administration of stripes, and one whose son or disciple dies under his chastisement)],
from My altar [if he were a Cohein and wished to perform the priestly service] shall you take him to die.
And if one strikes [and wounds] his father or his mother,
he shall be put to death [by strangulation (unlike one who wounds another, who pays but is not killed)].

And if one, [including a woman, tumtum (one of indeterminate gender) or hermaphrodite], kidnapped a man and sold him, and he were found in his hand, [i.e., men having witnessed his being kidnapped and sold and his having been in the kidnapper's hand before the sale],
he (the kidnapper) shall be put to death [by stoning].
And if one [including a woman] curses his father or his mother,
he shall be put to death [by stoning].

pairs.hebrew: וְכִֽי־יְרִיבֻ֣ן אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְהִכָּה־אִישׁ֙ אֶת־רֵעֵ֔הוּ בְּאֶ֖בֶן א֣וֹ בְאֶגְרֹ֑ף
pairs.english: And if men quarrel and a man strike his neighbor with stone or fist
and he not die, but become bedridden [and work-disabled],

pairs.hebrew: אִם־יָק֞וּם וְהִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ בַּח֛וּץ עַל־מִשְׁעַנְתּ֖וֹ וְנִקָּ֣ה הַמַּכֶּ֑ה
pairs.english: If he arise and walk outside on his own power, then the striker shall be absolved [(the striker being imprisoned pending resolution of the victim's state)];
only his work-disability [payment] shall he (the striker) give,
and heal shall he heal [i.e., he shall pay medical expenses].

pairs.hebrew: וְכִֽי־יַכֶּה֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶת־עַבְדּ֜וֹ א֤וֹ אֶת־אֲמָתוֹ֙ בַּשֵּׁ֔בֶט וּמֵ֖ת תַּ֣חַת יָד֑וֹ
pairs.english: And if a man strike his [Canaanite] man-servant or maid-servant with a rod [of killing potential], and he die under his hand,
vengeance [by the sword] shall be taken.
But if one day or two days [i.e., one day which is like two days, a twenty-four hour period] he survive,
vengeance shall not be taken, for he (the man-servant) is his money, [but if another (i.e., not his master) kills him, even if the servant lingered on that long, he (the murderer) is put to death].

pairs.hebrew: וְכִֽי־יִנָּצ֣וּ אֲנָשִׁ֗ים וְנָ֨גְפ֜וּ אִשָּׁ֤ה הָרָה֙ וְיָצְא֣וּ יְלָדֶ֔יהָ וְלֹ֥א יִהְיֶ֖ה אָס֑וֹן
pairs.english: And if men fight [with each other and one strikes at the other] and they hit a pregnant woman, and her fetuses miscarry, and there be no death [in the woman],

pairs.hebrew: עָנ֣וֹשׁ יֵעָנֵ֗שׁ כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֨ר יָשִׁ֤ית עָלָיו֙ בַּ֣עַל הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה
pairs.english: then he shall be punished [i.e., payment (for the fetuses) shall be exacted of him.] As the husband of the woman imposes upon him (the striker) [through beth-din]
he shall give by word of the judges.
And if there be death [in the woman]
then you shall give a life for a life [(According to one view, "life," literally; according to another, monetary payment, estimated by the sales-price of servants in the marketplace)].
An eye for an eye [(If one blinded another, he pays him the monetary value of an eye, estimated by loss of value of a blinded servant in the marketplace)];
a tooth for a tooth;

pairs.hebrew: יָ֚ד תַּ֣חַת יָ֔ד רֶ֖גֶל תַּ֥חַת רָֽגֶל׃
pairs.english: a hand for a hand; a foot for a foot.
A burn [produced by fire] for a burn [(monetary payment, estimated by how much one would give to be spared the pain of the burn)];
a wound [(where blood is drawn)] for a wound [(Though he makes the other payments (loss of limb, disability, etc.,) he is not exempt from payment for pain)];
a welt [(where no blood is drawn)] for a welt.

pairs.hebrew: וְכִֽי־יַכֶּ֨ה אִ֜ישׁ אֶת־עֵ֥ין עַבְדּ֛וֹ אֽוֹ־אֶת־עֵ֥ין אֲמָת֖וֹ וְשִֽׁחֲתָ֑הּ
pairs.english: And if a man strike the eye of his [Canaanite] man-servant or the eye of his maid-servant, and he destroy it,
free shall he send him in lieu of his eye [or any other organ prominences which do not grow back (excluding a child's tooth)].
And if the tooth [(though one is not born with it, unlike "eye")] of his man-servant or the tooth of his maid-servant he strike out,
free shall he send him in lieu of his tooth.

pairs.hebrew: וְכִֽי־יִגַּ֨ח שׁ֥וֹר אֶת־אִ֛ישׁ א֥וֹ אֶת־אִשָּׁ֖ה וָמֵ֑ת
pairs.english: And if an ox [(or any other animal)] gore a man or a woman and he die,

pairs.hebrew: סָק֨וֹל יִסָּקֵ֜ל הַשּׁ֗וֹר וְלֹ֤א יֵאָכֵל֙ אֶת־בְּשָׂר֔וֹ
pairs.english: the ox shall be stoned and its flesh shall not be eaten [even if it is slaughtered after judgment has been pronounced upon it],
and the owner of the ox is absolved ["the owner" of a tam (an ox that is not "confirmed" in killing, as opposed to a mued, a three-time killer ox. See 29)]

pairs.hebrew: וְאִ֡ם שׁוֹר֩ נַגָּ֨ח ה֜וּא מִתְּמֹ֣ל שִׁלְשֹׁ֗ם
pairs.english: And if it were a goring ox from yesterday and the day before,

pairs.hebrew: וְהוּעַ֤ד בִּבְעָלָיו֙ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁמְרֶ֔נּוּ וְהֵמִ֥ית אִ֖ישׁ א֣וֹ אִשָּׁ֑ה הַשּׁוֹר֙ יִסָּקֵ֔ל וְגַם־בְּעָלָ֖יו יוּמָֽת׃
pairs.english: [three gorings (including the latest), and the owner were warned [in the presence of witnesses], and he did not guard it, and it killed [(by goring or otherwise)] a man or a woman, the ox shall be stoned, and its owner, too, shall die [at the hands of Heaven].
When kofer ["atonement" (payment)] is set for him,

pairs.hebrew: וְנָתַן֙ פִּדְיֹ֣ן נַפְשׁ֔וֹ כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־יוּשַׁ֖ת עָלָֽיו׃
pairs.english: he shall give the redemption of his soul [(According to one view, the value of the victim; according to another, the value of the owner)], according to all that shall be set for him.
Or if it gore a son [a minor], or it gore a daughter [a minor],
according to this ordinance shall it be done to him.
If the ox gore a [Canaanite] man-servant or maid-servant,
then silver, thirty shekels, shall he give to his master [regardless of how much he is worth]
and the ox shall be stoned.

pairs.hebrew: וְכִֽי־יִפְתַּ֨ח אִ֜ישׁ בּ֗וֹר א֠וֹ כִּֽי־יִכְרֶ֥ה אִ֛ישׁ בֹּ֖ר וְלֹ֣א יְכַסֶּ֑נּוּ
pairs.english: And if a man open a pit [(in the public domain) which was covered] or if a man dig a pit [even if he completes another's digging], and he not cover it,
and there fall into it an ox or an ass [or any other animal],

pairs.hebrew: בַּ֤עַל הַבּוֹר֙ יְשַׁלֵּ֔ם כֶּ֖סֶף יָשִׁ֣יב לִבְעָלָ֑יו
pairs.english: the owner of the pit [i.e., the one who occasioned the damage, whether or not he be the actual owner] shall pay. Money shall he restore [(any kind of "restoration," even bran)] to its owner,
and the carcass shall belong to him [the latter (as partial payment towards damages)].
And if the ox [a tam ("non-confirmed" in damaging)] of a man strike [(any kind of "striking" — butting, kicking, biting, etc.)] the ox of his neighbor, and it die,
then they shall sell the living ox and halve its money [between them]
and also the [value of the] carcass shall they halve [between them (so that the owner of the tam, where both oxen are of equal value, pays half-damages)].

pairs.hebrew: א֣וֹ נוֹדַ֗ע כִּ֠י שׁ֣וֹר נַגָּ֥ח הוּא֙ מִתְּמ֣וֹל שִׁלְשֹׁ֔ם וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמְרֶ֖נּוּ בְּעָלָ֑יו
pairs.english: Or [if it were not a tam, but] it be known that it were a goring ox [a mued] from yesterday and the day before, [three gorings (including the latest)], and its owner did not guard it,
then pay shall he pay, an ox [full value] for an ox,
and the carcass shall belong to him [the owner of the gored ox, (the owner of the goring ox making up the difference between the value of the carcass and the full value of the gored ox)].

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֤י יִגְנֹֽב־אִישׁ֙ שׁ֣וֹר אוֹ־שֶׂ֔ה וּטְבָח֖וֹ א֣וֹ מְכָר֑וֹ
pairs.english: If a man steal an ox or a lamb, and slaughter it or sell it,
then five (head of) cattle shall he pay for the ox,
and four sheep for the lamb, ["ox" and "lamb," specifically (Only four for the lamb, as opposed to five for the ox, for the thief suffers shame in carrying the lamb (whereas he leads the ox)].
If the thief be found breaking in, and he be struck (by the owner) and die,
he (the owner) has no blood [liability, the thief coming with intent to kill the owner if necessary, and "If one comes to kill you, arise and kill him!"]

If the sun shone upon him [i.e., If it is obvious that the thief would not kill him (as in the instance of a father stealing from a son)], he (the thief) "has blood" [i.e., he is regarded as a "live man," and one who kills him is a murderer.]
Pay shall he [the thief] pay [for what he stole (but he is not to be put to death)].
If he lacks it, he is to be sold for his theft.

pairs.hebrew: אִֽם־הִמָּצֵא֩ תִמָּצֵ֨א בְיָד֜וֹ הַגְּנֵבָ֗ה מִשּׁ֧וֹר עַד־חֲמ֛וֹר עַד־שֶׂ֖ה חַיִּ֑ים
pairs.english: If the theft be found in his hand [i.e., in his possession, he neither having slaughtered it nor sold it], from ox to ass, to lamb [(all objects are included)], living (animals) [or their value, and not dead animals],
double shall he pay.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֤י יַבְעֶר־אִישׁ֙ שָׂדֶ֣ה אוֹ־כֶ֔רֶם וְשִׁלַּח֙ אֶת־בְּעִירֹ֔ה וּבִעֵ֖ר בִּשְׂדֵ֣ה אַחֵ֑ר
pairs.english: If a man take his beast into a field or a vineyard and he send his beast [and it tread, causing damage] or ravage [by the "tooth"] in the field of another,
then the best of his (the animal owner's) field and the best of his vineyard shall he pay [if he wishes to pay him in land].

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־תֵצֵ֨א אֵ֜שׁ וּמָצְאָ֤ה קֹצִים֙ וְנֶאֱכַ֣ל גָּדִ֔ישׁ א֥וֹ הַקָּמָ֖ה א֣וֹ הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה
pairs.english: If fire go out [even of itself] and it find thorns, and there be consumed [by the progress of the fire in the thorns] sheaves, or the standing corn, or the field, [his furrow being singed so that it has to be re-plowed],
pay shall he pay, he that lights the fire [even though he lights it in his own property and it moves of itself by means of the thorns].

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־יִתֵּן֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵ֜הוּ כֶּ֤סֶף אֽוֹ־כֵלִים֙ לִשְׁמֹ֔ר וְגֻנַּ֖ב מִבֵּ֣ית הָאִ֑ישׁ
pairs.english: If a man give to his neighbor money or vessels to watch [without pay], and it be stolen from the house of the man [(this being the latter's claim)],
if the thief is found, he shall pay double [to the owner].
If the thief not be found,
then the master of the house [where the article had been deposited] shall draw near to the judges [to deliberate with the owner and to swear to him]
that he has not sent his hand against his neighbor's deposit.

pairs.hebrew: עַֽל־כׇּל־דְּבַר־פֶּ֡שַׁע עַל־שׁ֡וֹר עַל־חֲ֠מ֠וֹר עַל־שֶׂ֨ה עַל־שַׂלְמָ֜ה עַל־כׇּל־אֲבֵדָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֹאמַר֙ כִּי־ה֣וּא זֶ֔ה
pairs.english: For every matter of offense, [where he is found to have lied under oath, witnesses testifying that he himself stole it, and the judges incriminating him on their testimony], for an ox, for an ass, for a lamb, for a garment, for every lost object about which he [the witness] will say that it is this [whereunto you swore that it was stolen, and, behold, you have it],
unto the judges, [who shall cross-examine the witnesses,] shall come the matter of both,
[and] whom the judges shall incriminate [i.e., the watcher, if he is found guilty], shall pay double to his neighbor.

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־יִתֵּן֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵ֜הוּ חֲמ֨וֹר אוֹ־שׁ֥וֹר אוֹ־שֶׂ֛ה וְכׇל־בְּהֵמָ֖ה לִשְׁמֹ֑ר
pairs.english: If a man give to his neighbor an ass or an ox or a lamb or any beast to watch [for pay],
and it die [naturally] or be broken or seized [by robbers], no one seeing [to testify to this],

pairs.hebrew: שְׁבֻעַ֣ת יְהֹוָ֗ה תִּהְיֶה֙ בֵּ֣ין שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם אִם־לֹ֥א שָׁלַ֛ח יָד֖וֹ בִּמְלֶ֣אכֶת רֵעֵ֑הוּ
pairs.english: the oath of the L-rd shall be between both, that he (the watcher) did not send his hand against the deposit of his neighbor [to use it for himself (for if he did, and it afterwards met with mischance, he is liable)],
and its owner shall accept [the oath], and he [the watcher] shall not pay.
And if it were stolen from him,
he shall pay its owner.
If it were torn [by a wild beast], let him bring witnesses [to that effect and thereby free himself of liability].
For the torn (beast) [(which he could not save, as when it was torn by a lion)] he shall not pay.

pairs.hebrew: וְכִֽי־יִשְׁאַ֥ל אִ֛ישׁ מֵעִ֥ם רֵעֵ֖הוּ וְנִשְׁבַּ֣ר אוֹ־מֵ֑ת
pairs.english: And if a man borrow from his neighbor and it be broken or die,
its owner not being with (i.e., engaged by) him [the borrower, in his work], pay shall he (the borrower) pay.
If its owner were with him [whether in the same work (as the animal) or some other work, even if he were not with him at the time of breaking or death], he (the borrower) shall not pay.

If it (the animal) were hired, it came by its hire [into the hands of the hirer, who, paying for it, (unlike the borrower), is not liable for mischance. (There is a difference of opinion as to whether he is to be regarded as an unpaid watcher or as a paid one.)]

pairs.hebrew: וְכִֽי־יְפַתֶּ֣ה אִ֗ישׁ בְּתוּלָ֛ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־אֹרָ֖שָׂה וְשָׁכַ֣ב עִמָּ֑הּ
pairs.english: And if a man entice a virgin who is not betrothed and he lie with her,
he shall endower her unto himself as a wife [i.e., he shall write her a kethubah (a marriage contract) and marry her.]
If her father refuse to give her to him,
money shall he pay [fifty shekels] as per the indemnity for the [ravished] virgins (see Deuteronomy 22:29)].
A witch
you shall not allow to live, [but you shall kill her, or him, as the case may be, (in beth-din)].
Anyone who lies with a beast [either actively or passively]
shall be put to death [by stoning].
One who slaughters
[(or performs any inner Temple service, like slaughtering) to idolatry shall be put to death — only to the L-rd alone!
And a stranger [from another land] you shall not taunt and you shall not oppress him [by theft],
for you were strangers in the land of Egypt [and are equally vulnerable to taunting].
Every widow and orphan
you shall not afflict. [All men are intended; it is just that "widow and orphan" are more vulnerable to affliction.]
If you afflict him, [you will receive your just deserts];

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י אִם־צָעֹ֤ק יִצְעַק֙ אֵלַ֔י שָׁמֹ֥עַ אֶשְׁמַ֖ע צַעֲקָתֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: for if he but cry out to Me, I will hear his cry.
And My wrath shall burn and I shall kill you by the sword,
and your wives will be widows, and your children, orphans [There will be no witnesses to your death, and your wives will not be able to remarry or your sons to inherit you.]
When you lend money, [lend it, preferentially, in this order:] My people [before heathens], the poor man [before the relatively wealthier] with you [in your city, before the poor of other cities].
Do not be to him as a creditor [Do not be severe in demanding payment. If you know that he is without means, act towards him as if you had not lent him.]
Do not impose interest (neshech) upon him, [neshech — "biting." Interest is like the biting of a snake. It begins with an almost imperceptible wound and then "swells" up to one's head.]
If you take as a pledge the garment of your neighbor [after the time for repayment of the loan arrives and he does not pay],
until the setting of the sun return it to him. [Scripture here speaks of a day garment, which is not needed at night. (Restore it for the day and you may take it again at night.)]

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י הִ֤וא כְסוּתֹה֙ לְבַדָּ֔הּ הִ֥וא שִׂמְלָת֖וֹ לְעֹר֑וֹ
pairs.english: For it is his solitary covering, [his outer garment]; it is his shirt for his skin [his inner garment].
On what shall he lie? [This includes his couch (as having to be returned for the day.)]
And it shall be, if he cries out to Me, I shall hear; for I am gracious.
Elohim you shall not curse [(an exhortation against cursing G-d and against cursing a judge)],
and a prince in your people you shall not curse.

Your fullness [the obligation that is incumbent upon you when your produce has fully ripened, i.e., bikkurim (first fruits)] and your dema (terumah) you shall not delay [you are not to change the order of their separation. You are not to take terumah before bikkurim or ma'aser before terumah].
The first-born of your sons you shall give to Me [(Redeem him from the Cohein for five sela'im)].

Thus shall you do with your ox, with your sheep [i.e., Just as a human bechor is redeemed after thirty days, so the bechor of small cattle (e.g., sheep) is to be looked after for thirty days and then given to the Cohein.]
Seven days shall it be with its mother [(an exhortation to the Cohein not to sacrifice it before the eighth day)];
on the eighth day you may give it to Me.
And [if] men of holiness [i.e., If you separate yourselves from abominations of neveilah and treifah], you shall be unto Me [i.e., you shall be Mine; if not, you shall not be Mine.]
And flesh torn [by a predatory animal from a live clean animal] in the field [(not necessarily the field, "the field" being the common instance)] you shall not eat;

to the dog you shall throw it [or you may sell it to a heathen ("the dog" being mentioned to indicate that it takes precedence to selling and also that "the Holy One Blessed be He does not withhold the reward of any creature" (see 11:7)].
Do not bear a false report [(an exhortation against receiving slander and an exhortation to a judge not to hear the words of one litigant before the other arrives)].

pairs.hebrew: אַל־תָּ֤שֶׁת יָֽדְךָ֙ עִם־רָשָׁ֔ע לִהְיֹ֖ת עֵ֥ד חָמָֽס׃
pairs.english: Do not place your hand with an evildoer [who puts forth a false claim against his neighbor] to [promise him to] be a false witness [for him].
Do not incline [in judgment] after many [wicked men, simply because they are many] for evil.

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹא־תַעֲנֶ֣ה עַל־רִ֗ב לִנְטֹ֛ת אַחֲרֵ֥י רַבִּ֖ים לְהַטֹּֽת׃
pairs.english: And do not answer [the defendant, who solicits your judgment] in the dispute, to incline after [those] many [wicked ones] to incline [the judgment from the truth; but judge in accordance with the truth and "let the collar (of responsibility) hang on the neck of the many"].
And do not honor a poor man
in his quarrel [to favor him in judgment simply because he is poor].

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י תִפְגַּ֞ע שׁ֧וֹר אֹֽיִבְךָ֛ א֥וֹ חֲמֹר֖וֹ תֹּעֶ֑ה
pairs.english: If you encounter the ox of your foe, or his ass, straying,
return shall you return it to him.
